title: Bacon and cabbage with parsley sauce

ingredients.name: savoy cabbage, cored and cut into wedges

steps: If the bacon is very salty, soak it in cold water for several hours or overnight, then drain.
Put the joint in a large pot with the onion and carrots, cover with fresh cold water and bring to the boil. Skim off the foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for about 20 minutes per 500 g plus another 20 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes to the pot for the last 25 minutes, and the cabbage wedges for the last 10 minutes.
For the sauce, melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Stir in the parsley and season with pepper.
Lift out the joint, rest it for 10 minutes and slice. Serve with the cabbage, potatoes, carrots and sauce.

title: Barmbrack (tea-soaked fruit loaf)
steps: Put the dried fruit and sugar in a bowl, pour over the hot tea, stir, cover and leave to soak overnight.
Heat the oven to 150 degrees C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Stir the beaten egg into the soaked fruit mixture.
Fold in the flour and mixed spice until just combined, without overmixing.
Spoon the batter into the tin and level the top.
Bake for about 1 hour 15 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool on a rack and serve sliced and buttered.

title: Carrageen moss pudding (set milk dessert)

ingredients.name: dried carrageen moss (or 1/2 tsp agar powder as a substitute)

steps: Soak the carrageen moss in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse it.

Put the moss and milk in a saucepan and bring slowly to a simmer. Cook gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the milk has thickened slightly and the moss is soft and gelatinous. If using agar, simmer for 2 minutes instead.
Strain the milk into a bowl, pressing out the thick jelly from the moss, and stir in the sugar and vanilla.
Beat the egg yolk into the mixture and whisk the egg white to soft peaks. Fold the whites in.
Pour into small dishes and chill for at least 3 hours until set.
Serve cold with stewed fruit or berries.

title: Chicken fillet roll (Irish deli-counter crispy chicken roll)

ingredients.name: chicken breast fillets, halved horizontally to make thin cutlets

steps: Season the flour with the salt and pepper. Pound the chicken lightly so it is an even thickness.
Coat each piece in flour, dip in egg and press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels.
Split the rolls and spread with mayonnaise, then add lettuce, grated cheese and the hot chicken.
Close the rolls and serve, with coleslaw or fries if you like.

title: Crubeens (boiled and breaded pig's trotters)
steps: Scrub the trotters well and put them in a large pot with the onion, carrot, bay leaves, peppercorns and salt.
Cover with cold water, bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours until the meat is tender and nearly falling from the bone.
Lift out the trotters carefully and cool them, then chill for at least 2 hours so they firm up.
Dust the trotters in flour, dip in beaten egg and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to about 170 degrees C and fry the trotters for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and crisp and heated through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mustard and bread.

title: Goody (bread boiled in sweet spiced milk)
steps: Warm the milk in a saucepan with the sugar and spice until just below boiling.
Drop in the torn bread and press it down into the milk.
Simmer gently, stirring and mashing, for 5 to 8 minutes until the bread has broken down into a soft, spoonable pudding.
Stir in the butter and serve warm in bowls, with a little extra sugar sprinkled on top.

title: Irish breakfast roll (sausage, bacon and egg in a crusty roll)
steps: Fry or grill the sausages for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until cooked through and browned.
Add the bacon rashers to the pan or grill for the last 5 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Fry the pudding slices, if using, for 2 minutes per side.
Fry the eggs in a little butter to your preferred doneness.
Split the rolls and butter them, then slice the sausages lengthways.
Fill each roll with sausages, bacon, pudding and an egg, add sauce and serve hot.

title: Irish coffee (hot coffee with whiskey and cream)
steps: Warm four stemmed glasses or mugs with hot water, then empty them.
Divide the sugar between the glasses and pour in the hot coffee, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the whiskey to each and stir.
Lightly whip the cream so it is thick but still pourable.
Pour the cream gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top of the coffee.
Serve immediately without stirring, drinking the coffee through the cream.

title: Irish salmon pie (poached salmon in cream sauce under mashed potato)
steps: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Poach the salmon in the milk with the bay leaf for 8 minutes until just cooked. Lift out, flake the fish and keep the milk.
Melt the 30 g butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the strained poaching milk and simmer until you have a thick sauce.
Fold in the flaked salmon, herbs and lemon juice and season. Spoon into a baking dish.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining butter and milk and season to taste, then spread over the salmon and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.

title: Nettle soup (spring soup of young nettles and potato)

ingredients.name: young nettle tops, picked with gloves (or spinach)

steps: Wearing gloves, wash the nettle tops and remove any thick stalks.
Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the onion and leek for 8 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Add the nettles and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Boiling removes the sting.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream and season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg.
Reheat gently without boiling and serve with brown bread.

title: Potato farls (griddle-fried potato bread triangles)

ingredients.name: floury potatoes, peeled and cut up
plain flour, plus extra for dusting

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, drain well and mash until completely smooth.
Stir in the melted butter and salt, then work in the flour to form a soft dough. Do not overwork it.
Turn out onto a floured surface and roll or pat into a round about 1 cm thick.
Cut the round into four triangular quarters.
Heat a dry non-stick frying pan or griddle over medium heat and cook the farls for 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Serve warm with butter, or fry in butter alongside bacon and eggs for breakfast.

title: Spice bag (Dublin takeaway crispy chicken, chips and peppers)

ingredients.name: curry sauce or sweet chilli sauce

steps: Mix the cornflour with half the five spice, chilli powder and salt, then toss the chicken strips in the mixture until coated.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large frying pan and fry the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Wipe out the pan, heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the peppers, onion and chillies over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until just softened.
Return the chicken and tip in the hot chips.
Sprinkle over the remaining spice mix and toss everything together.
Serve in a paper bag or bowl with curry sauce or sweet chilli sauce.
